page: Microsoft Azure B4s_v2 is a burstable general purpose virtual machine running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provides 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Memory configuration includes 16.0 GB of RAM, offering a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction support spans AVX, AVX-512 (including AVX512F and AVX512_VNNI), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI for cryptographic and vector processing tasks. The instance does not include bundled local disk storage or dedicated hardware GPUs, relying instead on network-attached remote storage, and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent single-threaded performance paired with constrained multi-core throughput typical of burstable resource allocations. In stress-ng, single-core CPU throughput reached an average 1894.89 points, while multi-core performance scored 3869.77 in the lower 25% bracket. Geekbench mirrors this divergence with a single-core score of 1674.0 and a multi-core score of 3558.0. Large-block memory bandwidth registers at 29.32 GB/sec for uncached reads and 25.64 GB/sec for uncached writes. Synthetic tests including PassMark CPU (5954.41) and Clang software compilation (4228.0) reflect multi-threaded limits stemming from the dual-core hyperthreaded physical layout.

The primary operational tradeoff of the B4s_v2 involves its burstable CPU allocation profile. Sustained multi-threaded execution experiences throttling once burst credits are depleted, as demonstrated by the weak multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 19.7 GB/sec and lower-tier database operation scores. However, average performance in static web serving throughput (6.42 GB/sec), small-model LLM text generation (111.91 tokens/sec), and PassMark encryption (3658.04) confirms solid per-core capability during baseline or burst periods.

Microsoft Azure B4s_v2 offers high resource cost efficiency for environments characterized by variable activity patterns. The 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides adequate capacity for development environments, low-to-medium traffic web servers, microservices, small in-memory caches, and non-continuous CI/CD runners that do not require sustained 100% CPU utilization.
description: Microsoft Azure B4s_v2 is a burstable general purpose virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor (x86_64) running at 2.8 GHz. It is provisioned with 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores and 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB per core. The server includes no local disk storage or dedicated GPUs. In synthetic evaluations, the instance posts competitive single-core throughput, such as a Geekbench single-core score of 1674.0 and PassMark encryption performance of 3658.04, but multi-core throughput is constrained by its shared burstable CPU model and physical core count. Static web serving throughput reaches 6.42 GB/sec. Given its burstable execution characteristics and balanced memory allocation, the B4s_v2 is an economical fit for development sandboxes, low-traffic web serving, microservices, and general compute jobs with intermittent processor demand.
